text:
ashwin (support): Heads-up — AcmeCorp escalation. Their /v1/generate calls from hosted API are seeing intermittent 502s and a few 504s since ~2026-03-15T09:12 PDT. They say traffic is ~90 rps with short bursts up to 250 rps, prompts large (~1.2k-1.8k tokens). Customer trace id: trace-ACME-7742. They sent curl repro.
ops-bot: PROD alert: edge-gw envoy cluster "hosted-api-upstream" 502 spike. 09:13:07 → 09:18:55. Metric: 502_rate 8.3% over 5m. Related svc: edge-proxy (us-west-2).
maria (eng-sre): I'm on it. Can someone paste the customer curl + headers and a sample envoy log line? Also curious whether this aligns w/ recent TCP keepalive change we pushed yesterday.
ashwin (support): Pasting customer repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"<~1500 token payload>","max_tokens":512}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Response intermittently: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway or sometimes 504 Gateway Timeout. Latency when 200: 120-250ms.
leo (eng-runtime): Adding envoy upstream log snippet we saw in logs for trace-ACME-7742:
```
[2026-03-15T16:14:11.123Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 NR - 0 0 0 - "trace-ACME-7742" "envoy" "upstream reset: connection aborted"
[2026-03-15T16:14:11.124Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 UPGRADE_FAILED - 0 0 0 - "trace-ACME-7743" "envoy" "upstream response timeout"
```
Note: NR/NORMAL codes show upstream connection reset and occasional upstream timeout.
sarah (eng-platform): Quick hypothesis: h2 connection pool to model-serving tier is getting stressed by large payloads + many concurrent streams. We recently tightened the keepalive and reduced max concurrent H2 streams per connection in the envoy config to lower memory usage. That could lead to faster pool churn and resets under bursty large requests.
jen (eng-oncall): Repro notes from customer: they hit the issue reliably if they run 3 clients each at ~80 concurrent requests with long payloads. If they add a small delay between chunks it stabilizes. I can reproduce locally in staging with a sim: 200 concurrent 1.5k-token requests -> intermittent 502s in the gateway.
maria (eng-sre): Good repro. Can we capture upstream socket errors from the edge nodes? Also check if the upstream (model-serving) logged any OOMs or 503s. leo, do we have per-connection reset counts by node?
leo (eng-runtime): Pulling counts — edge-node-7 shows a spike in "stream_reset_by_peer" and "connection_failure" counters around 09:14. Upstream model-pool nodes didn't show OOM but had increased accept queue length briefly. Configs: envoy h2 max-concurrent-streams set to 100 (global), keepalive interval 30s (new change). Before change it was 250.
dan (product-support): If this is config-related from yesterday, can we do a fast rollback of the keepalive/max-concurrent change for affected edge hosts? Customer is asking for ETA; they're threatening to reroute to competitor.
maria (eng-sre): I don't want a full rollback yet — we need targeted mitigation first. Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Temporarily bump max-concurrent-streams to 200 on edge nodes serving AcmeCorp's region (us-west-2) and increase h2 connection pool size for the cluster to reduce churn.
2) Add a route-level policy to pin that customer's requests to a smaller set of warm upstream connections (sticky). This reduces new conn establishment.
3) If we see errors continue, fallback to allowing HTTP/1.1 for that route as a last resort.
leo (eng-runtime): Config change I can push for step 1:
```yaml
clusters:
  - name: hosted-api-upstream
    http2_protocol_options:
      max_concurrent_streams: 200
    circuit_breakers:
      thresholds:
        - max_connections: 10000
```
I'll open a rolling config deploy to the three edge nodes in us-west-2 with canary 1/3 first.
jen (eng-oncall): Runbook note: when we see connection resets + NR, try increasing h2 streams and check upstream accept queue. oncall-bot linked runbook: https://internal/runbooks/edge-502-504
oncall-bot: Runbook reference posted: edge-502-504 -> steps, KB links, and rollback commands.
ashwin (support): I'll let the customer know we have a targeted mitigation plan and can do a config change within ~20-30 minutes. Also asking them to reduce client-side concurrency as a temporary workaround.
maria (eng-sre): After leo pushes canary, monitor 502 rate and stream_reset counters. If 1/3 canary looks good in 10m, roll remainder. Also watch model nodes for accept queue and latency.
leo (eng-runtime): Canary pushed to edge-node-5 (1/3). Initial telemetry: 502 rate dropped from 8.3% to 1.2% for that node within 2 minutes. stream_reset_by_peer decreased by ~70%.
maria (eng-sre): Great. Rolling to nodes 6 and 7 now.
leo (eng-runtime): Roll completed. Post-roll metrics: cluster-wide 502s down to 0.9% over 10m window. No upstream OOMs. Accept queue lengths normalized.
dan (product-support): Customer updated: They see 200s again and are running a longer soak test. They asked what the permanent fix will be.
sarah (eng-platform): Permanent plan: revert the aggressive keepalive/max-concurrent reduction, and implement adaptive h2 stream controls per-client based on payload length. Also add better early-backpressure (429) for huge simultaneous requests to protect the pool.
maria (eng-sre): I'll write a follow-up incident note and schedule a config rollback patch that implements conservative defaults + adaptive controls. Action items: leo to create infra PR for default max_concurrent_streams=200, sarah to design adaptive controller, jen to update runbook, ashwin to confirm customer closure once soak passes.
ashwin (support): Thanks everyone — sharing this with AcmeCorp now. I'll mark this escalated ticket as "mitigated - monitoring" and will reopen if errors reappear. :thumbsup:
jen (eng-oncall): leaving postmortem template here. We'll fill in root cause as "h2 connection pool churn due to lowered max-concurrent-streams + bursty large payloads" unless further evidence suggests otherwise.
oncall-bot: Incident channel summary created: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-3142
maria (eng-sre): Closing notes: short-term mitigation successful; tracking long-term fix in ENGPLAT-452. If anyone sees a reappearance ping me.
ashwin (support): Customer confirmed stable after 45m soak. Closing thread. Thanks all.
